[[](https://www.instagram.com/ruminati_au) ruminati_au Why are emissions reporting standards being developed? Not to add complexity, but to reduce fragmentation. Right now, similar farm information is requested in different ways across supply chains, banks and programs. 😣 Different templates. 😖 Different assumptions. 😫 Different expectations. That creates duplication and uncertainty, especially when producers are already managing seasonal and financial risk! Shared frameworks aim to create a common structure for information. Not new farm practices. A common language. The intention is practical: 👉 Reduce repeated data requests 👉 Improve comparability between reports 👉 Help supply chains use real data instead of broad assumptions 👉 Make participation more predictable over time Large organisations now have mandatory climate reporting obligations, including supply chain emissions. Agriculture sits within that picture. Alignment at the reporting level helps reduce confusion at the farm level. This won’t happen overnight, but consistency is what reduces reporting friction in the long run. Preparation doesn’t lock you in. It simply means you’re ready when information is requested. Clarity takes time. Alignment reduces burden. #AustralianAg #AgEducation #FarmData #AgEmissions #AussieFarmers](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DV909SgzFoJ/?utm_source=popular_topic_grid)

# Our World In Data Cattle Slaughtered 2000 2007 Decrease
[[](https://www.instagram.com/ruminati_au) ruminati_au Most farms already track the information that matters. 👉 Production. 👉 Inputs. 👉 Efficiency. 👉 Change over time. These aren’t “emissions activities”. They’re just good management. What’s changing isn’t farming, it’s how existing information is organised so it can be understood beyond the farm gate. We know the shift can feel frustrating. Requests often arrive with different assumptions and not always much clarity about how the information will be used. But emissions reporting is built from information producers already manage: 👉 Livestock numbers and performance 👉 Fertiliser and fuel use 👉 Feed and pasture inputs 👉 Productivity outcomes over time From there, emissions are calculated across: 👉Scope 1: direct on-farm emissions 👉Scope 2: purchased energy 👉Scope 3: supply chain activity The goal isn’t to create new work. It’s to organise existing data so it can be reused when requests come in. That’s what preparation really means, not more reporting, just better structure. Good data has always been part of good farming. Now it just needs to travel a little further. 🏷 #AustralianAg #SustainableAg #FarmEmissions #FarmData #AussieFarmers](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DVe9syBzsNb/?utm_source=popular_topic_grid)

[[](https://www.instagram.com/sggroup.id) sggroup.id In the next ten years, farms that still rely on old methods will start to fall behind. The real problem is simple, large land areas are hard to monitor. Livestock wander out of bounds, but it's often only noticed when it's too late. This is where GPS collars start to become the solution. Area boundaries can be set directly from your phone, and livestock movement can be monitored in real-time. This technology is already used in more than 80 countries. That means the shift to technology-based monitoring systems is no longer a choice, it's a necessity. But field management alone isn't enough. Operations, inventory, and finances also need to be kept under control. Without that, the business will struggle to grow. And this is exactly the point where many farmers start falling behind without realizing it. The role of today's generation is crucial. Not just to carry on the old ways, but to become a bridge between experience and technology, starting with data literacy, beginning to use systems, and having the courage to level up. Because in the end, it's not the strongest who survive, but the ones who adapt the fastest. SG - C1 is here to help manage everything in one system that is more organized, measurable, and ready to scale up. 🌾📱 If you're curious about which part of your business system can start to be improved, we can have a casual chat about your current business situation. 👉 http://wa.me/+6285973145688](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DWWXU2FD_eP/?utm_source=popular_topic_grid)

steps.text:
**Scientific names of all aquaculture species that produced a measurable (> 0 t) tonnage in 2001 for the country that had the lowest total production (in tonnes) among the five “biggest‑decrease” cattle‑slaughter countries (2000 – 2007)**  

| Aquaculture species (FAO Year 2001) | Scientific name |
|-------------------------------------|-----------------|
| Atlantic salmon | *Salmo salar* |
| Rainbow trout | *Oncorhynchus mykiss* |

These two species were the only ones listed on FishBase’s FAO Aquaculture Production table for **the United Kingdom** that had a production value greater than zero in the year 2001, and the United Kingdom was the country with the lowest cumulative production‑tons among the five countries that experienced the steepest decline in cattle slaughter between 2000 and 2007 according to Our World in Data.
